A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, fact: Why (a) says the buttresses took the push of 'the heavy stone roof'. Gothic cathedrals usually had timber roofs above stone vaults, and the outward push came mainly from the stone vaults. The card says only 'heavy roof'. Say 'the heavy stone ceiling (vault) and roof', or keep the card's wording.

rejected.title: Gothic cathedrals
card: Gothic cathedrals were tall stone churches built in European towns from about the 1100s. They cost huge sums and often took decades to build, so they showed a town's wealth and its faith in God.
Pointed arches
arches that rise to a point, not a curve. They carried weight better than rounded arches, so walls could be taller.
Flying buttresses
stone supports built outside the walls. They took the push of the heavy roof, so the walls could hold large windows.
Stained glass
windows made of coloured glass. They let in light and often showed Bible stories, which people who could not read could still follow.
rejected.remember: Gothic features let walls rise high and fill with light, and the whole building showed a town's wealth and faith.

a.q: What did flying buttresses allow Gothic builders to do?
opts: Build tall walls with large windows
Make the roof out of lighter timber
Replace stone with coloured glass
Build churches without any arches
a.why: Flying buttresses took the push of the heavy stone roof from outside. This let the walls hold large windows. They did not replace stone or arches, because the cathedral was still built of stone with pointed arches.
a.clue: Think about what held up the roof from outside the walls.

b.q: A town in medieval France spent decades building a huge cathedral with tall windows of coloured glass. What did this most clearly show?
opts: The town had both wealth and strong faith
The town had no need for stone buildings
The town's people could all read the Bible
The town needed a fort to defend itself
b.why: A huge cathedral cost a great deal and took many years, so it showed the town's wealth. It was built as a church, so it also showed faith. The glass told Bible stories because many people could not read, so it does not show that everyone could read.
b.clue: Think about the cost of the building and why it was built.

wants.why: It lets students see the three Gothic features named on the card and the size of the building.
